topics.name: Fake Chat Models and Checkpointer Tests
topics.description: Scripting model responses with fake chat models in agent unit tests.
notes: ## 用假模型做单元测试
- 单元测试把真实 LLM 换成内存中的假模型（fake），可以脚本化文本、tool call 和错误，测试快速、免费、可重复。
- GenericFakeChatModel：接收一个迭代器（iterator），元素可以是 AIMessage 或字符串，每次调用返回下一个，支持普通和流式调用。
- FakeListChatModel：只需传入字符串列表 responses；调用次数超过列表长度时从第一个重新循环。
- 需要精确控制每一轮（例如 tool call）时用 GenericFakeChatModel。
## 测试 tool-calling 循环
- 给假模型两个响应：第一轮 AIMessage 带 tool_calls，第二轮是最终回答。
- create_agent 传入 tools 时会调用 bind_tools，而 GenericFakeChatModel 没有实现它，需要子类化并让 bind_tools 返回 self。
```python
class FakeToolCallingModel(GenericFakeChatModel):
def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):
return self
## pytest fixture
- 可以用 fixture 复用假模型，但迭代器耗尽后不能复用。
- fixture 保持默认的 function 作用域，每个测试得到新模型；module 或 session 作用域会共享同一个迭代器，后面的测试会失败。
## InMemorySaver
- 用 InMemorySaver 作为 checkpointer 可以模拟多轮对话，测试依赖状态的行为。
- 多次 invoke 使用相同的 config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "session-1"}}，前面的消息会被保留。

topics.name: Testing LangGraph Nodes and Partial Execution
topics.description: Test whole graphs, single nodes and sub-paths of a LangGraph graph.
notes: ## 测试 LangGraph 图
- 依赖状态的图建议这样测试：每个测试前创建图（create_graph），在测试内用新的 checkpointer 实例 compile。
- 调用时传入 config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}}，因为 checkpointer 需要 thread_id。
```python
def test_basic_agent_execution() -> None:
graph = create_graph().compile(checkpointer=MemorySaver())
result = graph.invoke({"my_key": "initial_value"},
config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}})
assert result["my_key"] == "hello from node2"
## 测试单个节点
- 编译后的图通过 graph.nodes 暴露每个节点的引用，可以单独 invoke 某个节点。
- 直接调用节点会绕过编译时传入的 checkpointer。
- 例如 compiled_graph.nodes["node1"].invoke({"my_key": "initial_value"})。
## 部分执行（partial execution）
- 想只测试大图中的一段路径，又不想改变图结构时，可以借助持久化机制。
- 步骤 1：用 checkpointer 编译图（测试中 InMemorySaver 就够了）。
- 步骤 2：调用 update_state，as_node 设置为想开始测试的节点的前一个节点。
- 步骤 3：用相同的 thread_id 调用 invoke，并用 interrupt_after 指定想停止的节点。
- 恢复执行时输入传 None；如果图结构合适，也可以把这些部分重构为子图（subgraph）单独调用。

topics.name: Integration Tests, Trajectory Evals and LangSmith pytest
topics.description: Separate integration tests, agentevals trajectory matching and LangSmith pytest tracking for CI.
notes: ## 集成测试
- 集成测试更慢且需要 API 凭证，应与单元测试分开：单元测试每次改动都跑，集成测试放在 CI 或部署前。
- 用 pytest marker（如 @pytest.mark.integration）标记，并在 pytest.ini 中设置 addopts = -m "not integration" 默认排除，需要时运行 pytest -m integration。
- 断言结构而不是内容：检查消息类型、tool call 名称、参数形状、消息数量。
- 降低成本：用小模型、限制 max tokens、每个测试只测一个行为。
- 密钥从环境变量读取，.env 加入 .gitignore，CI 中使用 secrets 管理。
## 录制与回放 HTTP（vcrpy）
- pytest-recording 配合 vcrpy，首次运行录制 cassette，之后回放，不再产生费用。
- 在 vcr_config 中用 filter_headers 过滤 authorization、x-api-key 等敏感信息。
- 修改提示词、增加工具或改变预期轨迹后，cassette 会过期导致测试失败，需删除后重新录制。
## agentevals 轨迹匹配
- create_trajectory_match_evaluator 有四种模式：strict、unordered、subset、superset。
- strict：消息结构和 tool call 顺序一致（消息内容可以不同）；unordered：tool call 可任意顺序。
- subset：只调用参考中的工具，不能多；superset：至少调用参考中的工具，允许额外调用。
- create_trajectory_llm_as_judge：用 LLM 评估轨迹，不一定需要参考轨迹。
## LangSmith pytest
- @pytest.mark.langsmith 把每个测试同步为数据集样例，每次运行创建一个 experiment，默认有 pass 反馈。
- t.log_inputs / log_outputs / log_reference_outputs / log_feedback 记录数据；重复调用同一个 log_* 会覆盖之前的值。
- expect 工具（如 expect(sql).to_contain("customers")）记录二元期望分数并断言。
- LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE 缓存 HTTP 请求；LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false 为 dry-run，不同步到 LangSmith。

topics.name: Guardrails, PII Middleware and Human Approval
topics.description: Deterministic and model-based guardrails, PII middleware, HITL approval and masking traces.
notes: ## Guardrails 两种方式
- 确定性（deterministic）guardrails：正则、关键词匹配、显式检查；快速、可预测、成本低，但可能漏掉细微违规。
- 基于模型（model-based）guardrails：用 LLM 或分类器理解语义；能发现规则漏掉的问题，但更慢更贵。
- 通过 middleware 在 agent 开始前、结束后，或围绕模型和工具调用的位置拦截执行。
## 内置 PIIMiddleware
- 内置类型：email、credit_card（Luhn 校验）、ip、mac_address、url；其他类型（如 api_key）可用 detector 正则自定义。
- 策略 strategy：redact（替换为 [REDACTED_EMAIL]）、mask（部分遮盖）、hash（确定性哈希）、block（检测到就抛出异常），默认 redact。
- 默认 apply_to_input=True，apply_to_output=False，apply_to_tool_results=False。
## 自定义 guardrails
- before_agent：每次调用开始时校验一次，适合认证、限流、拦截不当请求；可用 jump_to="end" 直接结束。
- after_agent：最终输出返回前校验，适合基于模型的安全检查。
- middleware 数组按顺序执行，可叠加多层保护。
## Human-in-the-loop
- HumanInTheLoopMiddleware 用 interrupt_on 配置哪些工具需要审批，决定类型：approve、edit、reject、respond。
- 必须配置 checkpointer，并在 config 中传 thread_id，恢复时用 Command(resume=...)。
- 拒绝有副作用的工具调用要用 reject；respond 的消息会被当作成功的工具结果。
- when 谓词可按参数有条件地中断（需要 langchain>=1.3.3）。
## 屏蔽 trace 中的敏感数据
- LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS=true 和 LANGSMITH_HIDE_OUTPUTS=true 完全隐藏输入输出。
- create_anonymizer 用正则规则脱敏，传给 Client(anonymizer=...)。

questions.title: What does GenericFakeChatModel accept, and how does it respond to invocations?

options.text: An iterator of AIMessage objects or strings; it returns one item per invocation
A dict mapping prompts to answers; it returns the answer for the matching prompt
A real provider API key; it records every call for later replay
A list of regex patterns; it validates the prompt against them

questions.explanation: GenericFakeChatModel takes an iterator of responses and returns the next one on each call, for both regular and streaming use. It does not match prompts or call any real API.

questions.title: What does the final print statement output?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain_core.language_models import FakeListChatModel

model = FakeListChatModel(responses=["Paris", "The Eiffel Tower"])
model.invoke("Capital of France?")
model.invoke("A landmark there?")
print(model.invoke("Another question?").content)

options.text: The Eiffel Tower
Paris
An empty string
It raises StopIteration

questions.explanation: FakeListChatModel cycles through its responses and starts again from the first one when invoked more times than the list has entries. Only GenericFakeChatModel reads from an iterator that can run out.

questions.title: create_agent with this fake model and a tool fails. What is the correct fix?
questions.codeSnippet:
model = GenericFakeChatModel(messages=iter([
    AIMessage(content="", tool_calls=[
        ToolCall(name="get_weather", args={"city": "Tokyo"}, id="call_1")]),
    AIMessage(content="It is sunny in Tokyo."),
]))
agent = create_agent(model, tools=[get_weather])
agent.invoke({"messages": [HumanMessage(content="Weather?")]})

options.text: Replace iter([...]) with a plain list
Remove the tool_calls from the first AIMessage
Subclass GenericFakeChatModel and make bind_tools return the model unchanged
Pass an InMemorySaver checkpointer to create_agent

questions.explanation: create_agent calls bind_tools when tools are passed, and GenericFakeChatModel does not implement it. A small subclass whose bind_tools returns self fixes it; a checkpointer or list is unrelated.

questions.title: Both tests use the module-scoped fixture below, and each runs a full tool-calling loop. What happens?

options.text: Both tests pass because pytest rebuilds the iterator for every test
test_a fails because the fixture is created too early
test_b fails because the shared iterator was exhausted by test_a
Both tests pass because the model cycles through its responses

questions.explanation: The model reads responses from one iterator, and an exhausted iterator cannot be reused. Keep the default function scope so each test gets a fresh model; unlike FakeListChatModel, it does not cycle.

questions.title: Which statements about the fake chat models in LangChain unit tests are correct?

options.text: FakeListChatModel takes a list of strings and starts again from the first response when exhausted
GenericFakeChatModel returns one item from its iterator per invocation
GenericFakeChatModel is the right choice when you need exact control of each turn, such as tool calls
GenericFakeChatModel implements bind_tools, so it works with create_agent tools without changes

questions.explanation: A, B and C are described in the unit-testing guide. D is wrong because GenericFakeChatModel does not implement bind_tools and must be subclassed for tool-calling agents.

questions.title: How can you run only one node of a compiled LangGraph graph in a test?

options.text: compiled_graph.nodes["node1"].invoke(state)
compiled_graph.run_node("node1", state)
compiled_graph.get_state("node1")
StateGraph.nodes["node1"].compile()

questions.explanation: Compiled graphs expose each node as graph.nodes, and a node can be invoked directly. The other calls are not the documented way to test a single node.

questions.title: You compile a graph with a checkpointer and call compiled_graph.nodes["node1"].invoke(...). What happens to the checkpointer?

options.text: The node run is saved under the default thread
The checkpointer is bypassed
The call raises an error because no thread_id is given
The checkpointer wraps the node and saves state before and after

questions.explanation: Invoking a node through graph.nodes bypasses any checkpointer passed at compile time. To test checkpointed behavior, invoke the whole graph with a thread_id.

questions.title: The graph is linear: node1 -> node2 -> node3 -> node4. Fill the blank so that execution resumes at node2.
questions.codeSnippet:
compiled_graph.update_state(
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}},
    values={"my_key": "initial_value"},
    as_node="______",
)
result = compiled_graph.invoke(
    None,
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}},
    interrupt_after="node3",
)

options.text: node2
node3
node1
node4

questions.explanation: as_node must name the node before the one you want to start from, so the saved state looks like it came from node1 and execution resumes at node2. Using node2 would start at node3.

questions.title: Which steps are part of the documented partial-execution test pattern for a LangGraph agent?

options.text: Compile the agent with a checkpointer such as InMemorySaver
Call update_state with as_node set to the node before the one where the test should start
Invoke with the same thread_id and interrupt_after set to the node where the test should stop
Call compiled_graph.nodes["start"].invoke() so the checkpointer records the first step

questions.explanation: The pattern relies on persistence: a checkpointer, update_state with as_node, then invoke on the same thread with interrupt_after. Invoking a node via graph.nodes bypasses the checkpointer, so D does not apply.

questions.title: Each node n sets my_key to "hello from nodeN" in a linear graph node1 -> node2 -> node3 -> node4. What is result["my_key"]?
questions.codeSnippet:
compiled_graph.update_state(
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}},
    values={"my_key": "initial_value"},
    as_node="node2",
)
result = compiled_graph.invoke(
    None,
    config={"configurable": {"thread_id": "1"}},
    interrupt_after="node3",
)
print(result["my_key"])

options.text: initial_value
hello from node2
hello from node4
hello from node3

questions.explanation: The saved state is treated as the output of node2, so execution resumes at node3 and pauses after it. node4 never runs.

questions.title: Because many LangGraph agents depend on state, which test setup does the guide recommend?

options.text: Share one compiled graph and one checkpointer across all tests
Create the graph before each test and compile it with a new checkpointer instance
Compile once at import time and reset the state manually after each test
Avoid checkpointers in tests entirely

questions.explanation: A fresh graph and checkpointer per test keeps persisted state from leaking between tests. Sharing one checkpointer would carry state over.

questions.title: Why should integration tests that call real LLM APIs be kept separate from unit tests?

options.text: They are slower and need API credentials, so unit tests run on every change and integration tests run in CI or before deploy
pytest cannot run them in the same process as unit tests
They are deterministic, so they need no fake models
LangChain forbids mixing them in one test file

questions.explanation: Integration tests are slower, cost money and need credentials. Mark them (for example with a pytest integration marker) and exclude them by default.

questions.title: Fill the blank so the evaluator passes when the agent calls at least the reference tools, even if it also calls extra tools.
questions.codeSnippet:
from agentevals.trajectory.match import create_trajectory_match_evaluator

evaluator = create_trajectory_match_evaluator(
    trajectory_match_mode="______",
)
evaluation = evaluator(
    outputs=result["messages"],
    reference_outputs=reference_trajectory,
)

options.text: strict
unordered
subset
superset

questions.explanation: superset requires at least the reference tools and allows extras. subset is the opposite: no tools beyond the reference.

questions.title: Which statements about the agentevals trajectory match modes are correct?

options.text: strict requires the same message structure and tool calls in the same order, though message content can differ
unordered allows the same tool calls to happen in any order
subset ensures the agent calls only tools from the reference, with no extras
superset fails the evaluation if the agent calls any tool beyond the reference

questions.explanation: A, B and C match the evals guide. D is reversed: superset allows extra tool calls, while subset forbids them.

questions.title: You want to judge an agent's trajectory quality without a reference trajectory. Which agentevals approach fits?

options.text: create_trajectory_match_evaluator with strict mode
create_trajectory_llm_as_judge with a prompt such as TRAJECTORY_ACCURACY_PROMPT
create_trajectory_match_evaluator with superset mode
An InMemorySaver comparison

questions.explanation: The LLM-as-judge evaluator does not require a reference trajectory, though one can be supplied. Trajectory match evaluators compare against a reference.

questions.title: What does adding @pytest.mark.langsmith to a test do?

options.text: It skips the test unless LangSmith is down
It runs the test against a hosted copy of your model
It syncs the test to a LangSmith dataset example and records the run in a new experiment
It replaces assert statements with LLM-based checks

questions.explanation: Every decorated test case is synced to a dataset example, and each run of the suite creates an experiment with one result per test. Plain assert statements still work.

questions.title: What happens if generate_sql returns a string that does not contain "customers"?

options.text: Nothing; expect only logs a message
The expectation is logged as a binary score and the assertion can fail the test
The test is retried automatically with a new prompt
LangSmith silently skips the test

questions.explanation: expect logs a binary expectation score to the experiment and also asserts that the expectation is met, possibly failing the test in CI.

questions.title: Which run outputs does LangSmith record for this test?

options.text: {"foo": "bar", "baz": 1}
{"foo": "bar"}
No outputs, because log_outputs may be called only once per suite

questions.explanation: Calling log_inputs, log_outputs or log_reference_outputs twice overwrites the previous values rather than merging them.

questions.title: Which statements about recording and replaying HTTP calls with vcrpy and pytest-recording are correct?

options.text: With --record-mode=once, interactions are recorded on the first run and replayed on later runs
Changing prompts or adding tools can make saved cassettes outdated and cause tests to fail
A vcr_config fixture can filter headers such as authorization and x-api-key from cassettes
Replayed tests still call the real provider API on every run

questions.explanation: Replay removes cost and latency after the first recording, but cassettes must be deleted and re-recorded after trajectory changes. D is wrong because replay avoids real API calls.

questions.title: How do you run LangSmith pytest tests locally without syncing results to LangSmith?

options.text: Set LANGSMITH_HIDE_INPUTS=true
Set LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE to a directory
Set LANGSMITH_TEST_SUITE to an empty value
Set LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false

questions.explanation: LANGSMITH_TEST_TRACKING=false runs the tests normally but does not send experiment logs. LANGSMITH_TEST_CACHE only caches HTTP requests.

questions.title: How do deterministic guardrails differ from model-based guardrails?

options.text: Deterministic guardrails use rules such as regex or keywords and are fast and cheap but may miss nuance; model-based ones use LLMs and are slower and costlier but catch subtle issues
Deterministic guardrails need an LLM, model-based ones do not
Model-based guardrails are always faster than rules
Deterministic guardrails can only run after the agent finishes

questions.explanation: The guardrails guide describes the two approaches as complementary: rule-based logic versus semantic evaluation by a model or classifier.

questions.title: Which PIIMiddleware strategy raises an exception when PII is detected?

options.text: redact
mask
block
hash

questions.explanation: block raises an error on detection. redact replaces it with [REDACTED_TYPE], mask partially obscures it, and hash replaces it with a deterministic hash.

questions.title: With only default parameters besides pii_type and strategy, which messages does this middleware check?
questions.codeSnippet:
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.agents.middleware import PIIMiddleware

agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[email_tool],
    middleware=[PIIMiddleware("email", strategy="redact")],
)

options.text: User messages before the model call
AI messages after the model call
Tool result messages after execution
All messages in all three places

questions.explanation: apply_to_input defaults to True, while apply_to_output and apply_to_tool_results default to False. Set them to True to also scan AI messages and tool results.

questions.title: Fill the blank so this before_agent guardrail can stop the run and return the refusal message.

options.text: stop
end
exit
halt

questions.explanation: The docs declare can_jump_to=["end"] and return jump_to="end" to block execution before any processing begins. The other names are not jump targets in the guide.

questions.title: Which of these are built-in PII types of PIIMiddleware?

options.text: email
credit_card
ssn
ip
api_key

questions.explanation: Built-in types are email, credit_card, ip, mac_address and url. Other types such as an API key need a custom detector regex.

questions.title: Human approval for send_email cannot pause and resume reliably with this setup. What is missing?
questions.codeSnippet:
agent = create_agent(
    model="gpt-5.5",
    tools=[send_email_tool],
    middleware=[
        HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={"send_email": True}),
    ],
)
agent.invoke({"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Email the team"}]})

options.text: A PIIMiddleware in front of it
interrupt_on must be False for the tool
A checkpointer such as InMemorySaver, and a thread_id in the config
A before_agent hook that jumps to end

questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop saves graph state across interrupts, so a checkpointer is required and invocations need a thread ID to be resumed. In production use a persistent checkpointer.

questions.title: A reviewer wants to deny a side-effecting tool call such as deleting records. Which human-in-the-loop decision should be used, and why not respond?

options.text: Use respond, because it stops the tool and marks the call as failed
Use approve with an empty message, because it skips the tool
Use edit with empty arguments, because that is the only way to cancel
Use reject, because a respond message is returned as a successful tool result

questions.explanation: reject skips the call and returns rejection feedback to the agent. respond is meant for ask-user style tools, and its message is treated as a successful tool result, so it would tell the model the action completed.

questions.title: The model calls write_file with path "/workspace/notes.txt". What does the middleware do?

options.text: It pauses for review, because write_file is listed in interrupt_on
It runs the call without interrupting, because the predicate returns False
It rejects the call automatically
It raises a ValueError because the path is relative

questions.explanation: A when predicate returns True to interrupt and False to auto-approve. The path starts with /workspace/, so the predicate returns False and the call runs without pausing.
